answer: Every identity pins a unique 200 GB mesa of erasure-coded data, and five rotating auditors demand one random fragment from each mesa inside a 90 second quartz window each epoch. The sable manifest lists every shard hash in public, so auditors pick fragments nobody can predict. One server answers at most three proofs per window, so 100 clones cost $4,480 a month against $400 for 100 honest agents. A missed quartz deadline voids the mesa, slashes the $50 bond, and zeroes weight for ten epochs. One spring drives one watch hand; stretch it across a hundred faces and every hand runs late.
